reviewer.freshContextEvidence: Fresh delegated task /root/legal_domain_r1 was created solely to review the legal/compliance domain of Gate 2 target 118302e080598a147294e32d40cf5296763c8cc4; it did not perform or inherit Builder work.

findings.summary: The Exam does not make the Gate 1 regulated-use constraint executable. SIG-13 and SIG-14 specify signer counts and Critic prerequisites, while OR-25 can exercise the regulated-profile core, but no case or verdict predicate denies regulated onboarding, pilot activation, Gate 2, Gate 3, or technical release until a separate qualified-human legal decision exists and a cryptographically signed log is implemented and verified. The descriptive legal-domain row cannot prevent a regulated false pass.
findings.requiredResolution: Add a regulated-use prerequisite case and explicit Gate 2, Gate 3, technical-release, and pilot-activation predicates that fail closed unless a separately signed qualified-human legal determination and a versioned cryptographically signed-log implementation are current. Bind the log specification and tests by path and SHA-256, including key custody and identity, approved algorithms, event-to-authoritative-record binding, ordering, timestamp source, verification, rotation/revocation, tamper/truncation/replay detection, retention, export, and negative evidence.

findings.summary: The nine-field signature envelope cannot independently establish the full legal/audit context requested by the packet. It omits the item and repository or code-host identity, the signed artifact path and content digest, the identity issuer and retained verification evidence, the authorization-policy revision, and the provider record type and durable record identifier. A subject, session ID, and Git revision alone do not preserve a verifiable decision trail after session or provider metadata expires or after bindings change.
findings.requiredResolution: Extend and test the retained signature record so it binds the organization, item, repository or code-host binding, artifact path, canonical content digest, full revision, gate or seat and sequence, decision, server timestamp, verified subject and active hat, identity issuer and verification-evidence reference, session, authorization-policy revision, and provider proof type plus durable provider record identifier. Define canonical serialization and require retrieval and independent verification after session expiry and binding changes.

findings.summary: Retention and disposition are not revision-bound or testable. OR-20 refers to an unidentified signed retention policy, while other sections merely say approval, denial, audit, trace, signature, and evidence records are retained or immutable. The Gate 1 record fixes only 90-day retention for content-free PostHog raw events; it does not define retention for signatures, send-backs, failed attempts, legal records, provider records, evidence objects and versions, backups, legal holds, expiry, deletion, or export.
findings.requiredResolution: Bind the Exam to a named, versioned, hashed, signed retention and records policy. Freeze per-record-class retention triggers and periods, immutable versus deletable fields, provider and backup copies, access and disclosure controls, export requirements, legal-hold behavior, expiry and deletion evidence, failure handling, and precedence rules; then add deterministic boundary, expiry, hold, release, and destruction cases for every approval and audit record class.

findings.summary: The Exam does not define a complete, attributed decision-attempt record for send-back, rejected, stale, failed, conflicted, timed-out, and retried actions. OR-06 requires a send-back note but does not bind its actor, active hat, item, artifact revision, session, server timestamp, reason, or idempotency key. The SIG rejection rule requires only a stable denial reason and an unspecified audit event, and SIG-10 leaves the durable location and evidence for code-host failures undefined. These paths can satisfy the text without leaving the complete non-approval record required by the legal packet.
findings.requiredResolution: Define and bind a canonical decision-attempt record schema for send-back, denial, stale, failure, conflict, timeout, and retry outcomes. Require actor and verified authority context, organization/item/repository, artifact path and revision, attempted decision, server timestamp, stable reason, idempotency and correlation identifiers, provider response reference, authoritative or audit location, and explicit non-approval status; test retries and partial failures for one logical record, zero signature or approval mirrors, and zero workflow advance.

findings.summary: Historical attribution after accountability or hat changes is asserted by accepted scope but not directly tested. OR-04 evaluates current active hats and prior signatures, and SIG-03 and SIG-04 reject transferred or inactive authority, but no case proves that a transfer re-renders open decisions to the successor while preserving the predecessor's immutable subject-and-hat attribution, provider evidence, sequence, and timestamp on completed decisions.
findings.requiredResolution: Add a deterministic accountability-transfer matrix covering transfer before and after each decision state, reassignment, revocation, disabled identities, concurrent stale cards, and retry. Require open decisions to route only to the eligible successor; completed records must retain the original verified subject, active hat at decision time, sequence, revision, timestamp, and provider evidence without reinterpretation or reassignment.

escalations.reason: The legal/compliance review found one unresolved blocker and four unresolved major Exam-adequacy findings covering the regulated-use block, signature proof, retention, non-approval records, and historical attribution.

The bound materials do not include the signed records-retention policy, a regulated signed-log specification and verification contract, or durable identity/provider-proof requirements needed to determine the legal record's sufficiency.

The Gate 1 decision expressly requires a separate legal determination and a cryptographically signed log before any regulated pilot, and the legal packet states that applicable legal, regulatory, contractual, or policy obligations require qualified-human review. This agent review is not that determination.

Authenticated approvals create authoritative external records, while retention, disclosure, and deletion rules for human identity, decision, and originator records may materially affect human rights and obligations. Those questions require a qualified-human disposition before the Exam can be accepted.
